title: Why EDI managers are critical to AI-ready growth
summary: EDI managers are becoming key players in AI-ready growth. See how modern B2B integration builds the trusted data foundation AI needs to succeed.
body_markdown:
For many EDI managers, success used to be straightforward. If orders, invoices, and shipping documents moved without disruption, the job was getting done. But now, given the complexity of modern supply chains, EDI managers are pulled in many directions while navigating[ERP modernization projects](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/erp-integration-and-transformation) , partner ecosystem growth, mergers and acquisitions, cloud adoption, evolving customer requirements, and increasing pressure to automate and use AI. EDI is no longer a back-office function, but a strategic enabler of business agility, visibility, and innovation.


## The job of managing EDI has become far more complex


OpenText understands every new trading partner, customer requirement, compliance mandate, application, and communication standard makes the integration landscape more difficult, making you responsible for:


- Supplier and customer communities
- New partner onboarding initiatives
- Multiple EDI document types, APIs, and connectivity standards
- Evolving security and compliance requirements
- Expanding[ERP](https://www.opentext.com/what-is/erp-integration) , API, and cloud integration needs


Unfortunately, many businesses still rely on aging integration processes and technologies that were designed for a much simpler business environment. The result is increased manual work, slower onboarding, limited supply chain[visibility](https://www.opentext.com/what-is/supply-chain-visibility) , and greater operational risk.


## Modern EDI is more than compliance


For years,[EDI](https://www.opentext.com/what-is/electronic-data-interchange) was often viewed as something businesses had to do rather than something that created competitive value. If documents were exchanged accurately and customer requirements were met, few people thought much about it. That mindset is changing.


Compliance remains important, but the goal now is to enable a connected business ecosystem that helps organizations respond faster to change, operate more efficiently, and unlock new opportunities for growth and innovation. More importantly, modern integration creates a trusted foundation of connected data that supports analytics, automation, and future AI initiatives.


## AI is only as good as the data foundation behind it


Nearly every business is exploring how AI can help improve productivity, decision-making, and operational efficiency. But many organizations quickly discover that implementing AI isn’t the hard part. Giving AI access to accurate, connected business data is often the bigger challenge. If AI is built on a fragmented foundation, insights are limited and productivity gains are minimal.


As more AI initiatives get underway, many businesses are learning that valuable information remains trapped across ERP systems, partner networks, supply chain applications, spreadsheets, and disconnected integration environments. Without connected, accessible, and[trusted data](https://www.opentext.com/what-is/data-governance) , AI initiatives struggle to deliver meaningful business value.


## Where modern B2B integration plays a critical role


[B2B integration](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/b2b-data-exchange-and-integration) is like the connective tissue between your applications, trading partners, and business processes. When these systems work together, teams gain a clearer view of operations, processes become easier to automate, and issues such as exceptions, errors, and chargebacks can be addressed before they have a bigger impact.


That connectivity is also becoming an important part of AI readiness. AI can only be as effective as the data it can access, making integrated business networks a critical advantage. For EDI managers, this means their role is expanding beyond supporting transactions and day-to-day operations. They are increasingly helping build the data foundation that enables smarter automation, better business intelligence, and successful AI initiatives.


For EDI managers, this means[B2B integration](https://www.opentext.com/solutions/b2b-data-exchange-and-integration) is no longer simply supporting business operations but helping enable AI strategy.


## Most businesses face the same challenges


It’s easy to assume these legacy integration issues belong primarily to large enterprises. Small and midsized businesses often face the same EDI requirements,[connectivity needs](https://www.opentext.com/products/business-network-cloud) , customer demands, and supply chain disruptions. The difference is that they typically have fewer people and resources available to manage them. As complexity increases, even a small integration team can find itself stretched thin.


The difference is that smaller teams often have even less capacity to manage their integration ecosystem. Modern integration platforms and managed services can help level the playing field by providing enterprise-grade connectivity, automation, visibility, and expertise without requiring large internal teams.


## The future of EDI is connected, intelligent, and AI-ready


EDI isn’t going away. The role of the EDI manager is evolving. In fact, as businesses exchange more business information than ever before, reliable solutions like OpenText™[B2B Integration Enterprise,](https://www.opentext.com/products/b2b-integration-enterprise) OpenText™[B2B Integration Foundation](https://www.opentext.com/products/b2b-integration-foundation) , and OpenText™[B2B Integration Essentials](https://www.opentext.com/products/b2b-integration-essentials) become even more important. What’s changing is the role EDI software plays in an organization.


OpenText knows the future of EDI software isn’t simply moving transactions from point A to point B. It’s about:


- [Connecting and onboarding partners, applications, and business processes](https://www.opentext.com/products/b2b-integration-essentials) faster
- Improving supply chain visibility across your business
- Supporting ERP, EDI, and B2B modernization initiatives


## Building a trusted data foundation for AI and analytics


For EDI managers, that creates an opportunity to move beyond operational support and become a critical contributor to business modernization, EDI compliance, and[AI-ready growth](https://blogs.opentext.com/how-ai-is-shaping-the-future-of-edi/) .


As supply chains become increasingly connected and intelligent, businesses that will thrive are those that view EDI and B2B integration not as a compliance requirement, but as the digital backbone that enables visibility, automation, resilience, and innovation across the business ecosystem.
